clue.text: Country frequently gaining courage at present

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning current or up to date; the clue gives an adverbial phrase

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
oft is an old word for often
to have heart is to have courage

explanation.surface: A nation keeps growing braver in the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaining' simply strings the pieces together in reading order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something state-of-the-art is the latest available, reflecting technology as it stands right now.

clue.text: The man participating in binge, but skipping the last field

indicators.note: the man is participating in, that is inside, the shortened binge
skipping the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a spree is a binge
he is the man

explanation.surface: A man is joining a drinking session but leaves before the end of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field of activity or influence, as in one's sphere of expertise.

clue.text: Half of army enraged over having to transport ailing animal

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written, then halved

indicators.note: to transport something is to carry it within, so the other letters hold the ailing word

parts.note: enraged means mad
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: Half a furious army has to carry its sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an American mammal protected by bony armour plates.

clue.text: What about skill required to make electrical connection?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: eh? is said when asking someone to repeat themselves
an art is a skill, as in 'the art of persuasion'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the knack needed for wiring something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is not a question word here but the interjection EH, which goes round the skill word.
explanation.definitionFit: To earth an appliance, in British usage, is to wire it to the ground for safety (Americans say ground).

clue.text: See 8
Possibly works on log cabins, but not top part

indicators.note: in a down entry the top part is the opening letter, and it is to be dropped

parts.note: shacks are rough cabins; drop the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone may be doing woodwork on log cabins, though not the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs across 'log cabins' in the surface; it ends at 'log' and 'cabins' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping roughly at timber with an axe is hacking, one possible way to work on a log.

clue.text: Hallucinogen, a grass picked up by wild USA company

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue says the word for grass is read upwards

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: wild says the three letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American firm runs wild over a mind-altering grass.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY read upwards is YAH, and USA scrambled gives UAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayahuasca (spelt here with an O) is a psychoactive Amazonian brew that produces vivid visions.

clue.text: Cheers monarch showing some glamour?

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A toast to a rather glamorous king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' here means thank you, the British sense, which TA also has.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking is a dated adjective for attractive or charming, as in 'a taking smile'.

clue.text: Cursed line implying inadequate reflection by 15

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a line spoken under a curse, telling of a looking-glass that no longer reflects properly
setter's reading: the line is also a title by the crime writer at 15, Agatha Christie

annotation.spelling: THE MIRROR CRACK'D FROM SIDE TO SIDE

explanation.surface: A doomed verse line about a broken looking-glass, credited to a crime writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady of Shalott, in Tennyson's poem, cries that the curse is come upon her when her mirror breaks; Agatha Christie borrowed the line for a Miss Marple novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This verse from Tennyson's poem describes a cursed lady's glass splitting, and became the title of Christie's 1962 novel.

clue.text: Regular work putting out new diagram

indicators.note: to put something out is to eject it, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: the daily grind is routine work
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Routine office work stops producing fresh charts.
explanation.walkthrough: The routine-work word loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a pattern of crossing lines drawn as a chart or plan, so it is a kind of diagram.

clue.text: Garden equipment, embracing special garden equipment

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: hoes are weeding tools
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A shed of garden kit that includes some specialist kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'garden equipment' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second gives the tools that go round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoses are flexible pipes for watering beds and lawns, standard tools kept by gardeners.

clue.text: Painful, naturally, to have it cracked apart?

definitions.text: Painful, naturally, to have it cracked apart?

indicators.note: something cracked apart is split in two, so the letters straddle a break between words

parts.note: the last two letters of the first word plus the first two of the next

explanation.surface: A wry remark that breaking something in half naturally hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a forearm bone fracture is painful, and the bone itself is split across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of two long forearm bones, and fracturing it is, naturally, a painful injury.

clue.text: Nudity in California is cleaner

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a place in California
undress is a state of nakedness, as in in a state of undress

explanation.surface: Someone is naked in California and is a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nudity in California' reads as undress at LA, so LA comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose job is washing and ironing clothes and linen.

clue.text: Flag support for car workers' group at first

indicators.note: being placed at first puts this part ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: a trade union represents workers
a jack lifts and holds up a car

explanation.surface: A car workers' union flies the flag of its cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the jack first, but the workers' group goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Entirely so, when visiting English island

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so one piece enters another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
inch is a Scottish word for a small island
so and very both intensify, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: A tourist sees the whole of an English island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is not a whole one to visit but a Scottish word for an islet, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom meaning completely, as in 'every inch a gentleman'.

clue.text: Notorious murderer not getting money in exploitation of this crime

indicators.note: to exploit something is to work it over for gain, so the letters are worked into a new order
not getting something means going without it, so a letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A killer who never profits, though others cash in on his crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the M from THIS CRIME before rearranging. John Christie was a serial killer hanged in 1953 for murders at 10 Rillington Place, London.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reginald Christie is one of Britain's most infamous killers, so he fits a notorious murderer.

clue.text: Strain I avoided when touring US city to see author of 8/4

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened word goes around the city
avoided means the letter I is left out

parts.note: tension is strain
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A tired traveller avoids stress while touring an American city to see a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate and author of the cross-referenced work.

clue.text: Stop to offer special deal for bathroom goods?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: give up, concede defeat

definitions.text: offer special deal for bathroom goods
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: add a free bath item to a sale

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper pauses to run a promotion on bathroom stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to concede; a salesman 'throws in' an extra as a free bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in the towel is an idiom for quitting, and literally it describes adding a bath sheet free with a purchase.

clue.text: Heads for front in large movie cinema?

indicators.note: heads are the tops of things, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Audiences make for the front row at a huge picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movie' looks like the definition, but it is one of the four words supplying an opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Film, as an art form or industry, is another name for cinema, as in 'British film'.

clue.text: Staff sent up an amazing food

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers deliver an incredible dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the miraculous bread that fell from heaven to feed the Israelites in the wilderness, a truly astonishing provision.

clue.text: Good man engaged in negative statement, becoming this?

definitions.text: Good man engaged in negative statement, becoming this?

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be occupied inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
St, saint, is the usual abbreviation for a good man

explanation.surface: A decent person, stuck saying no, turns unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points back at the answer: a saint wrapped in a refusal becomes the word for unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps refusing in a mean way turns spiteful and unkind, which is what nasty describes.

clue.text: Source of heat, Sun, depicted by tattoos

definitions.note: in engineering a heat sink absorbs heat rather than producing it; the clue treats it loosely

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
ink is slang for tattoos

explanation.surface: A blazing sun motif shown in someone's body art.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the calendar abbreviation for Sunday. A heat sink is a component that draws warmth away from electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat sink is a finned metal part that soaks up warmth from a chip, so this is a looser fit than usual.

clue.text: Scene of witch-hunts and rough sex? Beer must be involved

indicators.note: something involved is caught up inside, so one piece is wrapped in the other

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of persecution, kinky sex and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer sits between the two letters of S&M.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem, Massachusetts, held the notorious witch trials of 1692, the most famous witch-hunt in American history.

clue.text: Language brought about by hardest landings

indicators.note: to bring a ship about is to turn it round, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pilots' bumpiest arrivals produce some strong words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought about' reads as 'caused', but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard English is the accepted, formal variety of the tongue used in education and print.

clue.text: Observe trace of repetition in most of new version

indicators.note: most but not all means the final letter goes
in places one thing within another

parts.note: a remake is a new version of a film, short its last letter

indicators.note: a trace is the smallest sign of something, so just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Spotting a hint of déjà vu in a film remake.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened remake word opens between its A and K to take the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to notice or comment on something, so it can mean to observe, as in 'he remarked her absence'.

clue.text: Sound of activity and energy, including a new kind

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a hum is the busy noise of things going on
E is the symbol for energy
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The buzz of a bustling place hints at a fresh sort of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like a noun meaning type, after 'new'; it is the adjective meaning compassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing compassion and mercy, a synonym for kind as in kind-hearted.
